utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good morning. Registrar, could you please call out the case number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, case number IT-97-25-I, the Prosecutor versus Milorad Krnojelac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. We may now commence with this hearing. As you know, this is the initial appearance of the accused before the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia, and it is being held in accordance with the Tribunal's Statute and Rules of Procedure and Evidence formally to charge the accused. Mr. Milorad Krnojelac, could you please rise and state for the Trial Chamber your name, date and place of birth, and the name of the attorney whom you have chosen to represent you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Milorad Krnojelac, born on the 25th of July, 1940 in the village of Birotici near Foca. I will be represented by Mihajlo Bakrac, an attorney. And today I'm represented by Mr. Toma Fila.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated. Could I please have the appearances for the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOWERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, Terree Bowers.

utterances.speaker: MS. THAPA
utterances.text: Tejshree Thapa.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Fila?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm Toma Fila. I will be representing Milorad Krnojelac today in this hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. As you know, the purpose of this initial appearance, and I just said this, is formally to charge the accused. The Trial Chamber is required to ensure that the indictment is read to the accused in a language he speaks or understands. If he waives his right to a public reading of the indictment, the Trial Chamber must, in any case, satisfy itself that he understands the indictment. We are then required to call upon the accused to enter a plea of guilty or not guilty on each count. If the accused fails to enter a plea, we are required by our Rules of Procedure and Evidence to enter a plea of not guilty on his behalf. In the case of a not guilty plea, we will instruct the registrar to set a date for trial. In the case of a guilty plea on all counts, we will instruct the registrar to set a date for the presentencing hearing or any other appropriate date. I would like to ask Defence counsel, Mr. Fila, whether he and his client have received copies of the indictment in a language that they understand and whether the contents therein were understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Your Honour, the accused has received not only the indictment but all the supporting material that he is supposed to have, that is, the statute and the rules of this Tribunal. I had a conversation with him today. He understood the indictment in its entirety. He waives his right to the reading, and he will just enter a plea of not guilty or guilty, and he understands in full the charges levied against him. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Fila, I understand that you had adequate time to confer with your client in preparation for this initial appearance?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Now, since, as you said, the accused, after consulting with you, is waiving his right to the public reading of the indictment, I will now recall each of the 18 counts against the accused. Mr. Krnojelac, could you please tell the court whether you plead guilty or not guilty after I have put the counts to you. The formal words we wish you to use is either "I plead guilty" or "I plead not guilty." Have you understood this?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I will start now with the various counts. Count 1: A crime against humanity, persecution on political, racial and/or religious grounds, punishable under Article 5(h) of the Statute of the International Tribunal. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Count 2: A crime against humanity, torture, punishable under Article 5(f) of the Statute of the International Tribunal. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Count 3: A grave breach, torture, punishable under Article 2(b) of the Statute of the International Tribunal. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Count 4: A violation of the laws or customs of war, torture, punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of the International Tribunal and recognised by Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Count 5: A crime against humanity, inhumane acts, punishable under Article 5(1) of the Statute of the International Tribunal. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Count 6: A grave breach, wilfully causing serious injury to body or health, punishable under Article 2(c) of the Statute of the International Tribunal. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Count 7: A violation of the laws or customs of war, namely, cruel treatment, punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of the International Tribunal and recognised by Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Count 8: A crime against humanity, namely, murder, punishable under Article 5(a) of the Statute of the International Tribunal. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Count 9: A grave breach, wilful killing, punishable under Article 2(a) of the Statute of the International Tribunal. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Count 10: A violation of the laws or customs of war in the form of murder, punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of the International Tribunal and recognised by Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Count 11: A crime against humanity, imprisonment, punishable under Article 5(e) of the Statute of the International Tribunal. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Count 12: A grave breach in the form of unlawful confinement of a civilian, punishable under Article 2(g) of the Statute of the International Tribunal. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Count 13: A crime against humanity in the form of inhumane acts, punishable under Article 5(i) of the Statute of the International Tribunal. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Count 14: A grave breach in the form of wilfully causing great suffering, punishable under Article 2(c) of the Statute of the International Tribunal. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Count 15: A violation of the laws or customs of war, namely, cruel treatment, punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of the International Tribunal and recognised by Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Count 16: A crime against humanity, namely, enslavement, punishable under Article 5(c) of the Statute of the International Tribunal. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Count 17: A grave breach in the form of inhumane treatment, punishable under Article 2(b) of the Statute of the International Tribunal. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Count 18: A violation of the laws or customs of war, namely, slavery, punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of the International Tribunal and recognised under the Slavery Convention and International Customary Law. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may now be seated. After the conclusion of this hearing, you will be remanded to the further custody of the International Tribunal and held in the detention unit until further order is made. Could I ask the registrar to please note the pleas of the accused? As the accused has pleaded not guilty to the charges against him, it is necessary to consider the organisation of the work of the Trial Chamber and the setting of the date for the trial. I wonder whether the registrar is able to set a date for the trial now?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, we are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Can you indicate a date?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Maybe after 60 days of preliminary motions, and then we can set a date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: So, therefore, we will await your confirmation. Now, of course, I don't need to remind both the Prosecution and the Defence of their obligations. In particular, the Prosecution, as we all know, has the duty to make available to the Defence all copies of the supporting material, in addition to what has already been handed, of course, to the accused; namely, you said the Statute and the Rules of Procedure. But what is needed for the Defence to receive from the Prosecution is the supporting material, namely, the material which accompanied the indictment when confirmation was sought and all the prior statements obtained by the Office of the Prosecutor from the accused. Of course, we all know, and I'm sure that Mr. Fila and the Prosecution are fully aware, that no later than 60 days before the date set for trial, copies of the statements of all witnesses whom the Prosecutor intends to call to testify must be made available to the Defence. I will not go into details on this matter because we are all familiar with these rules. May I ask now the Prosecution whether any such documents have already been provided to the Defence? If not, if the Prosecution may indicate a date by when those documents will be provided to the Defence, the supporting material for the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOWERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The confirmation material consists of approximately 47 witness statements. They have been redacted with regard to the other defendants/accused in this case, and they are ready to present to counsel. We would just request the court to issue the protective order with regard to those statements before we actually physically transfer them to the Defence. But they are prepared and can be turned over as soon as the protective order is in force.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Sorry. What sort of protective order, for the redaction, authorising you to redact the statements or protective measures?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOWERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's pretty much our standard protective order with regard to the witness statements that the Defence receives, that they will only use those in connection with the preparation of the Defence and not disclose them to the media. It's the same order that's been issued in prior proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right. So we will do so as soon as possible, maybe today or tomorrow, so that upon receiving this order, you may then be able to disclose all this material to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOWERS
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: So by when? Say, by next Monday, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOWERS
utterances.text: At the latest, hopefully sooner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Sooner, wonderful. So, Mr. Fila, you have taken notice of this pledge by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Yes, I fully agree that this should not be published. You know what my views are on publishing anything in the papers before the witness has testified. You know the case of a high ranking official. We read everything in the paper in Belgrade before he testified. I agree fully that this should be a principle of this Tribunal. I have been authorised to receive this material on Monday, regardless of whether my colleague, Mr. Bakrac arrives or not, because he has some problems with the visa, the usual problems with the visa. But I will be receiving the material on his behalf, and that's not a problem at all. So as far as the expediency is concerned, everything will be okay, and I agree fully that a date should be set now, but not before mid September. We really, all of us, the Defence counsel, we need our rest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes, we too actually, we Judges, because we are working very hard. I assume this also applies to the Prosecution. Generally speaking, you would be prepared to proceed to trial. Of course, I assume we can't set a date for trial now. It's very difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOWERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, just for the court's edification, this is a fully prepared case. We do not anticipate any significant amendment to the indictment. At the most, we would be possibly dropping the Article 2 counts to expedite the trial. It's fairly straightforward, and we are prepared to proceed whenever the court wishes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I see. Therefore, I think we should now think of a status conference. We should try to set a date for a status conference so that on that particular occasion, which will be held in closed session. Of course, as you know, that particular occasion, we could make all the necessary arrangements for the beginning of the trial which, as Mr. Fila rightly pointed out, in any case, cannot start before mid September, also because we have so many other cases. We are sitting, we, our Trial Chamber, we have six cases now, and probably so -- any suggestion about a date for the status conference?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: No problem. Whatever date is good for the Prosecution, I will make sure that my colleague is here. Although the court should set the date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: We would like to suggest a date which may be then set later on for mid August, the second part of August, because at that stage probably your colleague -- for the status conference, not for the beginning of the trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I'm sorry. But the Italians, they have their Ferragosto when everybody is on vacation. That's why I was laughing. I'm sorry, Your Honour, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: You know that we will start a new trial, Kupreskic, on the 17th of August, and we will go on, I think, for four weeks in a row sitting on Kupreskic. Well, Ferragosto is the 15th of August so, therefore, it is the -- we are sticking to the Ferragosto celebration. I wonder whether between the 17th of August and the end of August, this status conference could be held? You don't have, in principle, any opposition? We will let you know in due time, maybe in one week, which particular day is more convenient. All right? Any questions, any comments, any procedural matters? I wonder whether my colleagues have any questions to ask; no? All right, the hearing, then, may be adjourned. The hearing is adjourned.
